scope: Broaden comparison of open-source DWG/DXF implementations with source-backed failure-mode reports and Autodesk DXF processing guidance; map each signal to existing local plan owners without inferring a libdxfrw defect from peer behavior.

method.kind: Primary project issue/source and Autodesk documentation review
method.lineageRule: ACadRust and applications identifying it as their core CAD engine are one parser lineage, not independent parser votes.
method.evidenceRule: Peer issue reports and candidate commits establish a test lead scoped to their stated revision/corpus. They do not establish a libdxfrw defect, a normative DWG layout, a released peer fix, or semantic geometry validity.

evidence.observed: Autodesk guidance says not to depend on typical group-code ordering and notes future releases can add codes. It separately states repeated XDATA order is significant; group-0 records frame subsequent entities/objects.
doesNotEstablish: that every field may be reordered
that unknown group codes may be discarded in a preservation workflow
that parser success proves complete graph retention
evidence.planUse: Vary only order-independent fields; preserve XDATA, chunk, subclass and compound-child sequence; use following-record sentinels and explicit bounded raw/loss outcomes.

evidence.topic: Malformed DWG bounds, counts and allocation
evidence.observed: ACadRust issue reporters describe generated AC1024 inputs based on the peer's own writer. In 0.6.3, targeted mutations reportedly yielded over 100,000 zero-filled polyline vertices, an attempted roughly 12 TiB allocation, or a header-size slice panic. Issue activity links maintainer commits for record-bounded decoding and truncated-header handling, but does not publish a corpus retest or establish released behavior.
doesNotEstablish: a corresponding libdxfrw defect
that the candidate peer commits pass their complete regression corpus
that peer byte offsets are valid for libdxfrw-generated files
evidence.planUse: For any missing local coverage on a touched path, mutate one source-located field in a locally generated in-memory input; assert bounded disposition, no semantic zero-padding, no oversized reservation and intact framing.

evidence.topic: Unknown classes, named colors and table/block XDATA
evidence.observed: The 0.6.3 report distinguishes DXF-origin unknown/custom records lacking compatible DWG raw frames, DXF group-430 color-book names versus DWG DBCOLOR references, and table/block-record XDATA. A candidate commit and 0.6.4 release claims exist; the issue page does not publish a retest.
doesNotEstablish: that these behaviors are defects in libdxfrw
that DXF raw group codes are a valid DWG proxy frame
that color-book names and DBCOLOR handles are interchangeable
evidence.planUse: Keep opaque-frame, named-color-reference and table-XDATA conversion as distinct routes; require an explicit per-source disposition and avoid duplicating existing work items.

evidence.observed: The reporter describes a private 351-file corpus and an AC1032 case in which re-homing children of an absent anonymous dimension block reportedly creates 51 extra phantom model-space objects. A maintainer commit is linked, but no public corpus retest is shown and the drawings are unavailable.
doesNotEstablish: a libdxfrw orphan-recovery defect
that every absent owner should be dropped rather than reported or retained
full ownership correctness from equal total entity counts
evidence.planUse: Preserve the distinction among null/fixed-space, valid, unresolved non-null and orphan owners; never silently re-home a missing non-null owner into model space; compare by handle and logical block.

evidence.observed: Issue #134 reports strict-bound failures in AC1032 files after a peer release, concentrated in MLeader context objects, and links a candidate compatibility commit without a public private-corpus retest. Issue #135 reports AC1024 associative dependency records that are rejected in 0.6.4, decoded incorrectly in 0.6.3, and reportedly made Unknown on main; no drawing is attached. The reporters' proposed record-layout interpretations are hypotheses, not format authority.
doesNotEstablish: that libdxfrw has the same record layout or defect
that global record-bound checks should be softened
that Unknown output or successful document opening preserves the source object
evidence.planUse: Consult ODA v5.4.1 and a real traced sample before changing a parser. Separate outer frame truncation from bounded record-local auxiliary failure; require a following-object sentinel and visible typed/skipped/unknown outcome.

evidence.observed: Issue #136 reports 60 fixed-width call sites spanning 15 group codes in ACadRust 0.6.4 binary-DXF output, and says the same implementation's reader accepts its own malformed output. The round-trip test source also fabricates marker-bearing SAB and exercises the same implementation's writer/reader association path.
doesNotEstablish: that the reported binary widths are a libdxfrw defect
independent wire-format confirmation from a self-reader
valid ACIS topology from a marker-bearing fabricated SAB payload
evidence.planUse: Keep raw binary code/width parsing independent of the writer and reader under test. Treat fabricated SAB plus internal round-trip as structure/transport-only; require an independent eligible geometry consumer and shape invariants for semantics.

evidence.observed: ACadRust advertises broad version/entity coverage while its live issue tracker contains reports involving malformed input, conversion loss, ownership and version-specific object decoding. Open CAD Studio identifies ACadRust as its core engine, so it is not an independent parser vote.
doesNotEstablish: per-entity completeness from a version matrix or entity count
independence from the same parser lineage through a downstream application name
current behavior of an unpinned release or mutable main branch
evidence.planUse: Use one exact revision at the already planned composed checkpoint; record parser/consumer lineage, version, direction, options, per-handle disposition and diagnostics.

implementationReadinessChanges: Keep the current top implementation item: generate and structurally validate a nonempty AcDs data record, then bind record handle, modeler entity, owner and payload before enabling storage-backed replay.
Use the peer failure signals only as targeted negative/positive test patterns under existing owners; do not create duplicate findings or subplans.

Keep focused strict-build and generated-test checks per slice; run peer comparison at the existing composed checkpoint and retain full-suite, long fuzz/sanitizer and native CAD work at their scheduled gates.
Generate local controls in memory. Do not import peer/private drawings, reuse peer mutation offsets, add peer runtime dependencies, or commit new DWG/DXF fixtures.
